problems.quote: Reserve Bank of India — established under this act.
problems.problem: The Reserve Bank of India was established by the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934, not by the Government of India Act 1935.
problems.correction: Reserve Bank of India — established under the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934.
problems.verifierReason: RBI established by RBI Act 1934, not Government of India Act 1935. Correction is accurate.

problems.quote: North-Eastern Areas Reorganisation Act 1971 (Nagaland, Manipur, Meghalaya, Tripura, Mizoram, Arunachal)
problems.problem: Nagaland was not created by the 1971 Act; it became a state in 1963. The 1971 Act created Manipur, Meghalaya, Tripura as states and Mizoram, Arunachal as UTs.
problems.correction: North-Eastern Areas Reorganisation Act 1971 (Manipur, Meghalaya, Tripura, Mizoram, Arunachal)
problems.verifierReason: Original incorrectly includes Nagaland; 1971 Act created Manipur, Meghalaya, Tripura as states and Mizoram, Arunachal as UTs. Correction accurate.

problems.quote: The Supreme Court in State of West Bengal v. Union of India (1963) held that Parliament has the power to cede territory to a foreign country, but this requires a constitutional amendment (as held in t
problems.problem: The case State of West Bengal v. Union of India (1963) did not deal with cession of territory; the Berubari Union case (1960) established that cession requires a constitutional amendment.
problems.correction: The Supreme Court in the Berubari Union case (1960) held that cession of territory requires a constitutional amendment.
problems.verifierReason: State of West Bengal v. Union of India (1963) did not deal with cession; Berubari Union case (1960) correctly held cession requires constitutional amendment. Correction accurate.

problems.quote: In Union of India v. Rakesh Kumar (2023)
problems.problem: Wrong case name; the Supreme Court case on Article 370 abrogation is "In re: Article 370 of the Constitution" (2023).
problems.correction: In re: Article 370 of the Constitution (2023)
problems.verifierReason: The Article 370 judgment is correctly titled 'In re: Article 370 of the Constitution' (2023); 'Union of India v. Rakesh Kumar' is a different case.

problems.quote: The J&K Reorganisation Act retained a Legislative Assembly for the UT of J&K (90 seats + 5 nominated).
problems.problem: Incorrect number of nominated seats; the Act provides for nomination of two women members, not five.
problems.correction: The J&K Reorganisation Act retained a Legislative Assembly for the UT of J&K (90 seats + 2 nominated).
problems.verifierReason: J&K Reorganisation Act Section 14 provides for nomination of two women members, not five.

problems.quote: the states of Nagaland, Meghalaya, and Mizoram (have traditional tribal councils under the Sixth Schedule)
problems.problem: Nagaland is not under the Sixth Schedule; it has special provisions under Article 371A. The exemption applies to the whole states for varied reasons.
problems.correction: the states of Nagaland, Meghalaya, and Mizoram (which have special constitutional provisions and tribal councils)
problems.verifierReason: Nagaland is under Article 371A, not Sixth Schedule; Meghalaya and Mizoram have Sixth Schedule areas. Correction accurately covers all three.

problems.quote: prior consent of Gram Sabha for land acquisition
problems.problem: PESA requires consultation with Gram Sabha for land acquisition, not prior consent.
problems.correction: consultation with Gram Sabha for land acquisition
problems.verifierReason: PESA Section 4(i) mandates consultation with Gram Sabha for land acquisition, not prior consent.

problems.quote: Professional tax
problems.problem: Professional tax is levied by state governments, not a municipal revenue source.
problems.correction: Professional tax (state levy)
problems.verifierReason: Professional tax is a state levy under Article 276/Entry 60 State List, not a municipal revenue source.

problems.quote: Hyderabad (Telangana) — directly elected Mayor
problems.problem: The Mayor of Hyderabad is indirectly elected by corporators, not directly elected.
problems.correction: Hyderabad (Telangana) — indirectly elected Mayor
problems.verifierReason: Hyderabad Mayor is indirectly elected; correction accurately states this.

problems.quote: The 74th Amendment recommended the Nagarpalika Bill 1992 which provided for a directly elected Mayor with a fixed 5-year term
problems.problem: The 74th Amendment did not recommend the Nagarpalika Bill; the Bill was the precursor to the Amendment. Also, the Amendment does not mandate a directly elected Mayor; it leaves the manner of election to state legislatures.
problems.correction: The Nagarpalika Bill 1991 (which led to the 74th Amendment) proposed a directly elected Mayor with a fixed 5-year term, but the Amendment left the manner of election to state legislatures.
problems.verifierReason: 74th Amendment did not recommend the Bill; Bill was precursor. Correction fixes year and clarifies state discretion.

problems.quote: Pune, Nagpur (Maharashtra) — Mayor elected for 2.5 years (2018 reforms proposed direct election with 5-year term)
problems.problem: The 2018 reforms were enacted (Maharashtra Municipal Corporations (Amendment) Act, 2018) providing for direct election of Mayor for 5 years, not merely proposed. However, the law was later amended in 2019 to revert to indirect election.
problems.correction: Pune, Nagpur (Maharashtra) — Mayor elected for 2.5 years (2018 reforms enacted direct election with 5-year term, later reverted)
problems.verifierReason: 2018 Maharashtra reforms were enacted, not merely proposed; correction notes enactment and later reversion.

problems.quote: The Constitution provides five circumstances under which Parliament can legislate on subjects normally reserved for the States:
problems.problem: The text lists only four circumstances (Articles 249, 250, 252, 253) but mentions five. The fifth circumstance (Article 356 – President's Rule) is missing.
problems.correction: The Constitution provides five circumstances under which Parliament can legislate on subjects normally reserved for the States (including Article 356 during President's Rule).
problems.verifierReason: Constitution lists five circumstances (including Art. 356); original omitted it. Correction adds missing circumstance.

problems.quote: by a resolution supported by not less than 2/3 of the members present and voting in the Rajya Sabha, create one or more All India Services
problems.problem: All India Services are created by a law of Parliament, not by a Rajya Sabha resolution with a 2/3 majority
problems.correction: All India Services are created by an Act of Parliament
problems.verifierReason: All India Services created by Act of Parliament, not merely Rajya Sabha resolution; correction accurate.

problems.quote: on the recommendation of Lord Macaulay
problems.problem: The first Law Commission was established with Lord Macaulay as Chairman, not on his recommendation.
problems.correction: with Lord Macaulay as Chairman
problems.verifierReason: First Law Commission chaired by Macaulay, not established on his recommendation; correction accurate.

problems.quote: who drafted the Indian Penal Code (IPC) 1860, the Criminal Procedure Code, and the Civil Procedure Code
problems.problem: Lord Macaulay drafted the IPC; the Criminal Procedure Code and Civil Procedure Code were drafted by later commissions.
problems.correction: who drafted the Indian Penal Code (IPC) 1860
problems.verifierReason: Macaulay drafted only IPC; CrPC and CPC by later commissions; correction accurate.

problems.quote: The 22nd Law Commission (2020-2024) was chaired by Justice Ritu Raj Awasthi
problems.problem: The 22nd Law Commission's term was 2020-2023 (3 years), not 2020-2024.
problems.correction: The 22nd Law Commission (2020-2023) was chaired by Justice Rituraj Awasthi
problems.verifierReason: 22nd Law Commission term 2020-2023, chair Justice Rituraj Awasthi; correction fixes both.

problems.quote: The 23rd Law Commission was constituted in June 2025
problems.problem: As of 2024, the 23rd Law Commission has not been constituted; this is a future speculation.
problems.correction: The 23rd Law Commission is yet to be constituted
problems.verifierReason: As of 2024, 23rd Law Commission not constituted; original future date wrong; correction accurate.

problems.quote: the 22nd Law Commission submitted only 5 reports in its 4-year term
problems.problem: Law Commissions have a 3-year term, not 4 years.
problems.correction: the 22nd Law Commission submitted only 5 reports in its 3-year term
problems.verifierReason: Law Commissions have 3-year terms; original 4-year wrong; correction accurate.

problems.quote: Chairperson: Tuhin Kanta Pandey (since March 2025)
problems.problem: As of 2024, the SEBI Chairperson is Madhabi Puri Buch (since March 2022).
problems.correction: Chairperson: Madhabi Puri Buch (since March 2022)
problems.verifierReason: SEBI Chairperson as of 2024 is Madhabi Puri Buch; original future name wrong; correction accurate.

problems.quote: approximately 470 Articles
problems.problem: Incorrect number of articles; as of 2023 the Constitution has 448 articles.
problems.correction: 448 Articles
problems.verifierReason: Constitution has 448 articles as of 2023; 470 is incorrect.

problems.quote: The Rajya Sabha has equal representation for all States (not proportional to population), protecting smaller States.
problems.problem: Rajya Sabha representation is based on population, not equal.
problems.correction: The Rajya Sabha represents States with seats allocated roughly on the basis of population.
problems.verifierReason: Rajya Sabha seats allocated by population, not equal.

problems.quote: Unlike the USA and Australia (where there is dual citizenship — of the Union and of the individual State)
problems.problem: Australia has single citizenship, not dual citizenship.
problems.correction: Unlike the USA (where there is dual citizenship — of the Union and of the individual State), Australia has single citizenship.
problems.verifierReason: Australia has single citizenship; USA has dual.

problems.quote: The Constitution can be amended by simple majority for many provisions (creation of new States, salaries of judges, citizenship provisions, etc.).
problems.problem: These are not constitutional amendments; they are ordinary legislative acts under specific articles (e.g., Art. 3, 125, 11).
problems.correction: Many provisions (creation of new States, salaries of judges, citizenship provisions, etc.) can be changed by simple majority through ordinary legislation, not by constitutional amendment.
problems.verifierReason: Those changes are ordinary legislation, not constitutional amendments.

problems.quote: it has met only 12 times since 1990
problems.problem: The Inter-State Council has held 13 meetings as of 2022 (the 13th meeting was in 2022), not 12.
problems.correction: it has met 13 times since 1990
problems.verifierReason: ISC held 13 meetings by July 2022; quote stating 12 is outdated/incorrect.

problems.quote: ₹50 crore (fixed by Parliament)
problems.problem: The Contingency Fund of India is currently ₹30,000 crore (as per the 2021 amendment), not ₹50 crore.
problems.correction: ₹30,000 crore (fixed by Parliament)
problems.verifierReason: Original amount outdated; 2021 amendment raised it to ₹30,000 crore. Correction accurate.

problems.quote: Art 358 — Art 19 is automatically suspended (for duration of emergency).
problems.problem: Art 19 is automatically suspended only when the emergency is declared on grounds of war or external aggression, not for armed rebellion.
problems.correction: Art 358 — Art 19 is automatically suspended only if emergency is on grounds of war/external aggression.
problems.verifierReason: Art 358 suspends Art 19 only for war/external aggression emergencies per 44th Amendment. Correction correct.
